tools.name: todo_create
tools.description: Create a Todo. Optional priority: low, medium, high or urgent; omitted/null is unset. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

Owner.description:
An owner input: an explicit Actor, or `me`, an exact Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` or a canonical Agent id.
The Daemon resolves it before dispatch; stored owners are always Actors.

Actor.description: Who makes a call. `parent` is the Agent that started it, if any.

Priority.description: A Todo's optional urgency; unset is distinct from Low.

tools.name: todo_get
tools.description: Read one Todo. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

tools.name: todo_list
tools.description: List every Todo. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

tools.name: todo_update
tools.description: Change a Todo's title, body or priority. Priority: low, medium, high or urgent; omitted preserves it, null clears it. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: UpdateParams
inputSchema.description:
Changes title/body/priority. `expected_change` is the last captured History Change sequence;
mismatch is CONFLICT, a removed Todo is NOT_FOUND, and omission is unconditional.

priority.description: Omitted preserves priority; null clears it; otherwise low, medium, high or urgent.

Priority.description: A Todo's optional urgency; unset is distinct from Low.

tools.name: todo_complete
tools.description: Mark a Todo done. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

tools.name: todo_reopen
tools.description: Reopen a done Todo. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

tools.name: todo_setBlockers
tools.description: Replace a Todo's whole blocker list. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: SetBlockersParams
inputSchema.description:
Replaces the whole blocker list. A list that would make a cycle is an error.
`expected_change` is the last captured History Change sequence; mismatch is CONFLICT,
a removed Todo is NOT_FOUND, and omission is unconditional.

tools.name: todo_assign
tools.description: Assign a Todo to an owner, or leave it unassigned. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: AssignParams
inputSchema.description:
Sets the owner, `None` for Unassigned. `expected_change` is the last captured History Change
sequence; mismatch is CONFLICT, and omission is unconditional.

Owner.description:
An owner input: an explicit Actor, or `me`, an exact Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` or a canonical Agent id.
The Daemon resolves it before dispatch; stored owners are always Actors.

Actor.description: Who makes a call. `parent` is the Agent that started it, if any.

tools.name: todo_move
tools.description: Move a Todo into a Workstream, or out of every Workstream with a null `home`. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: MoveParams
inputSchema.description: Moves a Todo to a Workstream, or to the Project root when `home` is `None`.

tools.name: todo_reorder
tools.description: Put a Todo before another in the Todo order, or last with a null `before`. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: ReorderParams
inputSchema.description: Puts a Todo before another in the Todo order, or last when `before` is `None`.

tools.name: todo_delete
tools.description: Delete exactly the chosen Todo ids. Capture an operation key before calling; retry the same key and ids after an unknown reply. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: DeleteParams
inputSchema.description:
A caller-captured key binds one exact chosen set in its original Project.
Retry only with the same key and ids after an unknown transport outcome.

tools.name: todo_comment
tools.description: Leave a comment on a Todo only when the user must read it, such as a question or a blocker. Write one short plain line, at most 280 characters; it shows in the user's Inbox until they open the Todo. Never report progress or results here. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: CommentParams
inputSchema.description: Adds a comment to a Todo. The author is the calling Actor, never a param. An Agent's body is one line of at most 280 characters (T21).

tools.name: todo_comments
tools.description: Read a Todo comment thread oldest first, including authors and user replies. Reading does not mark comments read. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

tools.name: todo_addRef
tools.description: Point the user to a Pad or one section of it from a Todo, so they open it from the Todo and read it. Pass the link `roundup://pad/<name>?project=<key>`; a section link ends in `#<heading>`, the heading's text percent-encoded. The Pad and heading must exist. Adding the same link twice keeps one. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: RefParams
inputSchema.description: Adds or removes a link to a Pad or Pad section on a Todo (T27): `roundup://pad/<name>?project=<key>`, ending in `#<heading>` for a section.

tools.name: todo_removeRef
tools.description: Remove a Pad or Pad-section link from a Todo, by the same link you added; removing one the Todo lacks changes nothing. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: RefParams
inputSchema.description: Adds or removes a link to a Pad or Pad section on a Todo (T27): `roundup://pad/<name>?project=<key>`, ending in `#<heading>` for a section.

vendorHelp.edit:
Edit one or more issues within the same repository.

Editing issues' projects requires authorization with the `project` scope.
To authorize, run `gh auth refresh -s project`.

Use `--attach` to upload an image or video to a single issue. Without a body
flag the issue keeps the body it already has and the attachment is appended to it.
If the body references an attached file, such as `![alt](./login.png)`, that
reference is rewritten to point at the uploaded asset instead.
You can attach up to 50 files per command.

Alt text for an image follows the path after `#`, as in
`--attach './login.png#The login error state'`. Without it the filename is used.
A reference already in the body keeps the alt text written there. Video renders
as a player and has no alt text, so it cannot be given any.

If some attachments upload and others fail, the issue is still updated with the
ones that succeeded. The command then exits with a non-zero status, but the edited
issue URLs are still printed to stdout.

The `--add-assignee` and `--remove-assignee` flags both support
the following special values:
- `@me`: assign or unassign yourself
- `@copilot`: assign or unassign Copilot (not supported on GitHub Enterprise Server)


USAGE
  gh issue edit {<numbers> | <urls>} [flags]

FLAGS
      --add-assignee login         Add assigned users by their login. Use "@me" to assign yourself, or "@copilot" to assign Copilot.
      --add-blocked-by number      Add 'blocked by' relationships by issue number or URL
      --add-blocking number        Add 'blocking' relationships by issue number or URL
      --add-label name             Add labels by name
      --add-project title          Add the issue to projects by title
      --add-sub-issue number       Add sub-issues by number or URL
      --attach file                Attach an image or video file, in '<file>#<image alt text>' format
  -b, --body string                Set the new body.
  -F, --body-file file             Read body text from file (use "-" to read from standard input)
  -m, --milestone name             Edit the milestone the issue belongs to by name
      --parent number              Set the parent issue by number or URL
      --remove-assignee login      Remove assigned users by their login. Use "@me" to unassign yourself, or "@copilot" to unassign Copilot.
      --remove-blocked-by number   Remove 'blocked by' relationships by issue number or URL
      --remove-blocking number     Remove 'blocking' relationships by issue number or URL
      --remove-label name          Remove labels by name
      --remove-milestone           Remove the milestone association from the issue
      --remove-parent              Remove the parent issue
      --remove-project title       Remove the issue from projects by title
      --remove-sub-issue number    Remove sub-issues by number or URL
      --remove-type                Remove the issue type from the issue
  -t, --title string               Set the new title.
      --type name                  Set the issue type by name

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  $ gh issue edit 23 --title "I found a bug" --body "Nothing works"
  $ gh issue edit 23 --add-label "bug,help wanted" --remove-label "core"
  $ gh issue edit 23 --add-assignee "@me" --remove-assignee monalisa,hubot
  $ gh issue edit 23 --add-assignee "@copilot"
  $ gh issue edit 23 --add-project "Roadmap" --remove-project v1,v2
  $ gh issue edit 23 --milestone "Version 1"
  $ gh issue edit 23 --remove-milestone
  $ gh issue edit 23 --body-file body.txt
  $ gh issue edit 23 --attach './login.png#The login error state'
  $ gh issue edit 23 --attach ./before.png --attach ./after.png
  $ gh issue edit 23 34 --add-label "help wanted"
  $ gh issue edit 23 --type Bug
  $ gh issue edit 23 --remove-type
  $ gh issue edit 23 --parent 100
  $ gh issue edit 23 --remove-parent
  $ gh issue edit 100 --add-sub-issue 123,124
  $ gh issue edit 123 --add-blocked-by 200 --add-blocking 300,301

LEARN MORE

vendorHelp.comment:
Add a comment to a GitHub issue.

Without body text or attachments supplied through flags, the command will
interactively prompt for the comment text.

Use `--attach` to upload an image or video. If the body already references an
attached file, such as `![alt](./login.png)`, that reference is rewritten to point
at the uploaded asset. Any attached file the body does not reference is appended
to the end of the comment.
You can attach up to 50 files per command.

Alt text for an image follows the path after `#`, as in
`--attach './login.png#The login error state'`. Without it the filename is used.
A reference already in the body keeps the alt text written there. Video renders
as a player and has no alt text, so it cannot be given any.


USAGE
  gh issue comment {<number> | <url>} [flags]

FLAGS
      --attach file      Attach an image or video file, in '<file>#<image alt text>' format
  -b, --body text        The comment body text
  -F, --body-file file   Read body text from file (use "-" to read from standard input)
      --create-if-none   Create a new comment if no comments are found. Can be used only with --edit-last
      --delete-last      Delete the last comment of the current user
      --edit-last        Edit the last comment of the current user
  -e, --editor           Skip prompts and open the text editor to write the body in
  -w, --web              Open the web browser to write the comment
      --yes              Skip the delete confirmation prompt when --delete-last is provided

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  # Add a comment to an issue
  $ gh issue comment 12 --body "Hi from GitHub CLI"
  
  # Attach a screenshot, with alt text after "#"
  $ gh issue comment 12 --attach './login.png#The login error state'
  
  # Attach multiple files by repeating the flag
  $ gh issue comment 12 --attach ./before.png --attach ./after.png

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`
vendorHelp.close:
Close issue

USAGE
  gh issue close {<number> | <url>} [flags]

FLAGS
  -c, --comment string        Leave a closing comment
      --duplicate-of string   Mark as duplicate of another issue by number or URL
  -r, --reason string         Reason for closing: {completed|not planned|duplicate}

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  # Close issue
  $ gh issue close 123
  
  # Close issue and add a closing comment
  $ gh issue close 123 --comment "Closing this issue"
  
  # Close issue as a duplicate of issue #456
  $ gh issue close 123 --duplicate-of 456
  
  # Close issue as not planned
  $ gh issue close 123 --reason "not planned"
